name: Brazil

narrative.essence: Brazil hasn't won the World Cup since 2002 — their longest drought since they first appeared in the tournament. The ache is national, persistent, and politically charged. In 2026, with Vinícius Jr. at peak powers and a rebuilt squad, they believe the hexacampeonato is finally within reach.
narrative.footballIdentity: Brazil and football are synonymous. Pelé, Ronaldo, Ronaldinho — the Seleção didn't just win World Cups, they defined what football could be at its most joyous. Jogo bonito isn't a tactic, it's a national value. But since 2002, that joy has curdled into anxiety. The 2014 humiliation — 7-1 to Germany at home — still echoes. Every Brazilian squad carries that ghost into every tournament.
narrative.theMoment: Brazil enters 2026 in political and social turbulence. Lula's government faces deep polarization, and football has been dragged into the culture wars — Vinícius Jr., Brazil's biggest star, has been a lightning rod for racism in European leagues and a defender of progressive causes at home. Whether this squad can unite rather than divide a fractured country is as interesting as whether they can win. The hexacampeonato would be the binding agent Brazil's political class can't manufacture.

keyPlayers.name: Vinícius Jr.
keyPlayers.note: The most exciting attacker in the world right now. Explosive, creative, unstoppable in one-on-ones. This is his tournament to define his legacy.

keyPlayers.name: Rodrygo
keyPlayers.note: The big-game player. Scores in Champions League knockouts with regularity. Provides the technical complement to Vinícius' directness.

keyPlayers.name: Bruno Guimarães
keyPlayers.note: The best midfielder in the Premier League. Combines defensive intelligence with creative distribution — the engine room of everything Brazil does.

keyPlayers.name: Marquinhos
keyPlayers.note: Elite center-back with over a decade of top-level experience. Leads Brazil's defensive structure with intelligence and aerial dominance.

tactics.tacticalNote: Dorival's 4-2-3-1 gives Vinícius the freedom to run at defenders while Rodrygo provides technical quality on the opposite flank. Bruno Guimarães and a partner screen the defense while the number 10 connects midfield to attack. Brazil wants to control possession but can also explode in transition — the two modes are deliberately blended.
tactics.strength: Individual quality at every position — Brazil has arguably more stars on the field at once than any other squad in the tournament.
tactics.vulnerability: Defensive concentration in high-pressure moments — Brazil's backline can be disorganized when pressed by direct, fast opponents, as Qatar 2022 showed.

watchFor: Vinícius's acceleration on the left flank — one touch to set, one explosive burst to get to the byline. Defenders' hips must be perfect to stop him.
Bruno Guimarães pressing triggers — he leads Brazil's counterpresses with exceptional anticipation of where the ball will go.
Brazil's set piece threat — Marquinhos, Militão, and Gabriel Magalhães are all aerial dangers at corners and free kicks.
